Posted April 1, 2002

Coming to the Internet on April 15th --

After a great deal of thought, I am launching several new Internet sites, and reviving MarijuanaNews.com as a daily news service -- with a difference.

MarijuanaNews.com:

MarijuanaNews.com will have two features. The first will be a summary of the day's news, which will be the basis of a five-minute audio news, (five days a week) similar to the 420 MarijuanaHeadlineNews that I did on Pot-TV. (See section on TheVoiceofCannabis.com below.)

These written news summaries will be somewhat longer and more complete than the audio and will also include links to supporting material on MarijuanaNews.com and other sites.

The second part of MarijuanaNews.com will involve a greater focus on media criticism. This will include letters to the editors of publications which -- either in acts of omission or commission -- continue to prove my claim that the best two-word explanation of cannabis prohibition sadly remains " bad journalism. "

Of course, media criticism has long been a major part of MarijuanaNews.com. But now it is " no-more-Mr.-Nice-Guy. "

After almost a decade of

See

Of course, there is an enormous range in the quality or lack thereof in publications. But even those that have editorialized in favor of the legalization of cannabis often demonstrate a remarkable lack of journalistic standards when reporting on the subject.

I am not interested in their motives or their excuses. I can hardly begin to express my disgust with this malpractice but I am going to try! I hope that this will also develop into a book to bring the subject into sharper focus.

The new web sites ---

TheVoiceofCannabis.com:

TheVoiceofCannabis.com will be the platform for daily five minute audio news programs that I am going attempt to get on broadcast radio. There will be other audio features such as regular interviews with the leaders of the cannabis reform movement and newsmakers.

There may also be some Internet video programs, but the emphasis is going to be on audio because it is so much more economical. Also TheVoiceofCannabis.com will be frankly experimental in a way that could not be possible on Pot-TV or any other established platform.

TheVictimFiles.com:

Anther new site that I think will serve real a need will be called TheVictimFiles.com. This site will consist entirely of the stories of the victims of cannabis prohibition, under the header -- " Cannabis Prohibition is not a victimless crime. "

This site will be done in cooperation with NORML, which receives numerous horror stories from victims on a daily basis. However, victims will be invited to send their stories directly to TheVictimFiles.com as well. Although there are over 2,000 arrests everyday, not all of the stories would make interesting reading. Nonetheless, I anticipate that we will have sufficient material for daily postings. They can either be anonymous, with all identifying information omitted or with contact information for the victims if they so wish. I hope that this site will serve several purposes.

First, at a time when a Justice on the Supreme court can use the word " druggie " to describe someone who objects to mandatory urine testing of all students, it is essential to put the human face on the victims of state terror.

Second, victims need to tell their stories, perhaps only for catharsis, but also to reach out to others to get help or just to feel less alone.

However, I hope that TheVictimFiles.com will also serve to spur readers into joining NORML and becoming active in the cause of freedom. People should not wait until their stories are on TheVictimFiles.com to get active.

InternationalCannabis.com:

MarijuanaNews.com, TheVoiceofCannabis.com and TheVictimFiles.com all will be a part of InternationalCannabis.com which will initially serve only as a hub for these and other sites that will be created to support the cannabis reform movement. In time, as cannabis prohibition comes to an end, I hope to develop InternationalCannabis.com into a platform for legal cannabis related businesses.

InterNorml.org:

Last but not least, at the NORML conference I will be announcing the creation of a new international organization to be called InterNorml.

InterNorml will be a virtual organization devoted to encouraging greater international cooperation in the global cannabis reform movement. InterNorml will not attempt to impose any agenda on the various national groups seeking the legalization of cannabis, but will simply offer a focal point for international cooperation and communication which is now sorely lacking. Such an omission is inexcusable in the age of the Internet.

As noted, these sites are experimental and will be evolving as the need changes and the opportunities grow.

I hope to see as many of you as possible at the NORML conference in San Francisco, where I will be chairing

In any case, I will " see you on the Internet " on April 15th when these new sites go online.

Richard Cowan
